outcome: No proof or counterexample of the coefficient-free Baum–Connes conjecture for all discrete groups has appeared since 26 January 2024; the window holds class-level results (relatively hyperbolic groups with CAT(0) parabolics, December 2025; closed subgroups of real rank one groups, claimed December 2025), with-coefficients permanence results for extensions (2025–2026) including a published counterexample to a claimed simplification (August 2025), a finite-wreath-product variant (September 2025), and coarse, groupoid and Hecke-pair analogues, while the Wikipedia article (last edited 10 January 2026) still states that the conjecture without coefficients is open.
problem_asks: Read from the bullet alone: (a) the assembly map mu from the equivariant K-homology of the classifying space for proper actions of a discrete group G to the K-theory of its reduced group C*-algebra C*_r(G) is an isomorphism; (b) the bullet restricts no group class, so the claim is read as for every discrete group G (as the Wikipedia article reads it); (c) being an isomorphism, it asks for injectivity and surjectivity together, in every degree; (d) the bullet names no coefficient algebra, so the coefficient-free version (coefficient algebra C) is the reading the bullet supports, while the version with coefficients in a G-C*-algebra is a neighbouring question that the bullet does not name. No field or characteristic applies.

events.what_happened: Higson, Lafforgue and Skandalis, 'Counterexamples to the Baum-Connes conjecture', Geom. Funct. Anal. 12(2) (2002) 330–354. Using Gromov's monster groups (expander-based groups), they build short exact sequences of Γ-C*-algebras whose crossed products fail to be exact on K-theory; the result is that for a Gromov monster group Γ there are commutative Γ-C*-algebras A1, A2 such that the assembly map with coefficients in A1 is not injective, or with coefficients in A2 is not surjective. Wikipedia states the counterexamples are to the version with coefficients. Not opened: the paper is paywalled, and this summary rests on secondary sources (Wikipedia, Puschnigg's Bourbaki exposé, Skandalis's slides and a search listing).
events.delivers: Counterexamples to the Baum–Connes conjecture with coefficients (for suitable commutative coefficient algebras and Gromov monster groups). Per Wikipedia and the secondary sources, not a counterexample to the version without coefficients.
events.remains: The coefficient-free conjecture for all discrete groups (Wikipedia: 'The conjecture without coefficients is still open').
events.direction: Against the version with coefficients: the assembly map fails for some Gromov monster groups with some coefficient algebras. Silent on the coefficient-free version.
events.object: Gromov's monster groups Γ (groups containing expanders, not exact) with commutative Γ-C*-algebras A1 and A2 such that the assembly map with coefficients in A1 fails to be injective, or with coefficients in A2 fails to be surjective. The existence of the groups comes from Gromov's non-constructive construction; the coefficient algebras are not explicit in the sources I read.

events.what_happened: Higson and Kasparov, 'E-theory and KK-theory for groups which act properly and isometrically on Hilbert space', Invent. Math. 144 (2001) 23–74 (a 1997 announcement preceded it). Establishes the strong Baum–Connes conjecture, hence the version with coefficients, for groups with the Haagerup property (a-T-menable groups). Wikipedia lists this among the known cases. Not opened: the paper; the year and journal come from a search listing.
events.delivers: The conjecture, with coefficients, for all groups with the Haagerup property (a-T-menable groups). Restricted to that class.
events.remains: Groups without the Haagerup property, including property (T) groups such as SL(3,Z) (Wikipedia names SL(3,Z) as the simplest group where the coefficient-free conjecture is not known).
events.direction: Positive for the Haagerup class.

events.what_happened: Mineyev and Yu, 'The Baum-Connes conjecture for hyperbolic groups', arXiv:math/0105086 (first posted 10 May 2001); published Invent. Math. 149 (2002) 97–122 (journal from a search listing). The abstract says the paper proves the conjecture for hyperbolic groups and their subgroups; it does not say whether coefficients are included.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 10 May 2001; journal version Invent. Math. 2002.
events.delivers: The conjecture for hyperbolic groups and their subgroups (coefficient status not stated in the abstract).
events.remains: Groups outside the hyperbolic class and its subgroups.
events.direction: Positive for the hyperbolic class.

events.what_happened: Oyono-Oyono, 'Baum-Connes conjecture and extensions', J. Reine Angew. Math. 532 (2001) 133–149. Zhang's 2025 v2 cites it as a known result: if every finite-index overgroup of N in Γ and Γ/N satisfy the conjecture with coefficients, so does Γ. Not opened: the statement comes from Zhang's v2 text, not from the 2001 paper.
events.delivers: With coefficients: extension permanence under finite-index-overgroup and quotient hypotheses. Known result; not a new class.
events.remains: Extensions whose hypotheses are not verified.
events.direction: Positive, conditional.

events.what_happened: Wassermann's proof of the conjecture for real reductive groups, 1987, as cited in the Wikipedia article's list of known cases. Not opened: the original is not in my sources.
events.delivers: The conjecture for real reductive groups (Lie group case, not discrete groups as such).
events.remains: Discrete groups outside the cases listed in the Wikipedia article.
events.direction: Positive for the Lie group class.

events.what_happened: Chabert, Echterhoff and Nest, 2003, as cited in the Wikipedia article: almost connected groups and k-rational points of linear algebraic groups over local fields of characteristic zero. Not opened.
events.delivers: The conjecture for almost connected groups and k-rational points of linear algebraic groups over local fields of characteristic zero.
events.remains: Discrete groups outside these classes.
events.direction: Positive for these Lie-theoretic classes.

events.what_happened: V. Lafforgue, 1998, the conjecture for cocompact lattices in SL(3,R), as stated in the Wikipedia article. Not opened.
events.delivers: The conjecture for cocompact lattices in SL(3,R).
events.remains: Non-cocompact lattices, SL(3,Z) and the other higher-rank cases.
events.direction: Positive for these lattices.

events.what_happened: Baum, Guentner and Willett, 'Expanders, exact crossed products, and the Baum-Connes conjecture', arXiv:1311.2343 (first posted 11 November 2013; v2 6 August 2014; v3 21 April 2015); Annals of K-Theory 1(2) (2016) 155–208. Reformulates the conjecture with coefficients using a new crossed-product functor; all confirming examples for the original remain confirming; for exact groups the reformulation coincides with the original; some expander-based counterexamples become confirming examples. The same material was presented as talks (Guentner, Fields Institute, 2016; Baum, Fields Institute, 30 July 2026, 'There are no known counter-examples to the Baum-Connes conjecture'); these talks present the 2013 argument and are not separate results. The 2026 talk poses SL(3,Z) as an open question.
events.delivers: A reformulation of the conjecture with coefficients; no statement about the coefficient-free conjecture beyond the exact case, where the two coincide.
events.remains: The coefficient-free conjecture for all discrete groups, including non-exact groups where the reformulation differs.
events.direction: Reformulation; neither proves nor disproves the original.

events.what_happened: Osajda, 'Small cancellation labellings of some infinite graphs and applications', arXiv:1406.5015 (posted 19 June 2014; v3 17 May 2020; to appear in Acta Math., published 2020 per search listing). Constructs the first finitely generated groups with expanders embedded isometrically in their Cayley graphs, and the first finitely generated coarsely non-amenable groups without Property A that coarsely embed into Hilbert space. The abstract does not mention the Baum–Connes conjecture; that failures follow for these groups came from a secondary summary, which I did not verify.
events.delivers: Groups whose Cayley graphs contain isometric expanders; by a secondary summary, these are counterexamples to versions of the conjecture with coefficients or to coarse versions. The abstract itself states only the group-theoretic and coarse-geometric properties.
events.remains: Whether the coefficient-free group conjecture fails for these groups is not stated in what I read.
events.doubts: The Baum–Connes failure attributed to these groups rests on a secondary summary and is not stated in the arXiv abstract. The judging pass should not take it as established from this record.
events.direction: Group-theoretic construction; any bearing on the conjecture depends on the failure claim above, which I did not verify.
events.object: Finitely generated groups, built as infinite graphical small cancellation groups from infinite sequences of bounded-degree finite graphs, whose Cayley graphs contain expanders isometrically embedded. Explicit construction (small cancellation labellings); the expanders come from the sequence of graphs.

events.what_happened: Chung and Nowak, 'Expanders are counterexamples to the ℓ^p coarse Baum-Connes conjecture', arXiv:1811.10457 (first posted 26 November 2018; v2 23 August 2021; v3 17 June 2022); to appear in J. Noncommut. Geom. (DOI 10.4171/JNCG/498 on the arXiv page). They show the ℓ^p coarse Baum–Connes assembly map (1<p<∞) is not surjective for expanders arising from residually finite hyperbolic groups.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 26 Nov 2018; v2 23 Aug 2021; v3 17 Jun 2022.
events.delivers: Counterexamples to the ℓ^p coarse Baum–Connes conjecture; a coarse analogue, not the group conjecture.
events.remains: The group conjecture.
events.direction: Against the coarse analogue only.
events.object: Expanders built from residually finite hyperbolic groups, for which the ℓ^p coarse assembly map is not surjective. Construction details not read.

events.what_happened: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis, 'The Baum–Connes conjecture localised at the unit element of a discrete group', arXiv:1807.05892 (v1 16 July 2018; v2 9 September 2020; to appear in Compositio Mathematica). Builds a localised assembly map μ_τ in KK-theory with real coefficients; the τ-Baum–Connes conjecture is weaker than the classical one but still implies the strong Novikov conjecture.
events.delivers: A weaker, localised variant of the conjecture; not the conjecture itself.
events.remains: The classical statement.
events.direction: A variant; neither proves nor disproves the classical conjecture.

events.what_happened: Bönicke and Proietti, 'Categorical approach to the Baum–Connes conjecture for étale groupoids', arXiv:2202.08067 (v1 16 Feb 2022; v2 22 Feb 2022; v3 5 Dec 2023); J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 23(5) (2024) 2319–2364 (journal from the arXiv page). Localises the equivariant Kasparov category at weakly contractible objects; the resulting 'strong' Baum–Connes conjecture for étale groupoids implies the classical groupoid version; applications include split injectivity results for groupoids amenable at infinity.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 16 Feb 2022; v2 22 Feb 2022; v3 5 Dec 2023; JIMJ 2024.
events.delivers: A strong form of the conjecture for étale groupoids; groupoid setting, not discrete groups.
events.remains: The group conjecture.
events.direction: A groupoid-level strengthening; neither proves nor disproves the group conjecture.

events.what_happened: Julg, arXiv:1605.07408 (May 2016): constructs a Fredholm module representing the Kasparov gamma element for real rank one groups, described by Julg as the main step of his proof of the Baum–Connes conjecture for such groups. Not opened: the abstract is from a search listing.
events.delivers: A step in Julg's program for real rank one groups (with coefficients, per the program's aim); not a finished theorem in my sources.
events.remains: The rest of Julg's program, including the representation-theoretic and analytic conjectures.
events.direction: Positive step for real rank one groups.

events.what_happened: Julg and Nishikawa, 'Slow exponential growth representations of Sp(n,1) at the edge of Cowling's strip', arXiv:2106.10536 (posted 19 June 2021; v2 12 October 2022); later listed as J. Operator Theory 92(1) (2024) (journal from a search listing; not verified on arXiv). The abstract gives a slow exponential growth estimate for the spherical principal series of Sp(n,1) at the edge of Cowling's strip, and a homotopy estimate that the abstract says is required for Julg's program toward the conjecture with coefficients for Sp(n,1). It does not claim the conjecture itself.
events.delivers: A representation-theoretic estimate in Julg's program for Sp(n,1); not a Baum–Connes case by itself.
events.remains: The analytic conjecture (see the 2025 entry) and the Baum–Connes statement for Sp(n,1) as the abstract frames it.
events.direction: Step toward the conjecture for Sp(n,1) only.

events.what_happened: Deng and Toyota, arXiv:2509.06876 (September 2025): twisted coarse Baum–Connes conjecture for relatively hyperbolic groups; per a search snippet, G satisfies the twisted coarse conjecture for any stable coarse algebra if and only if each peripheral subgroup does. Not opened: this comes from a search snippet.
events.delivers: A coarse-geometric reduction for relatively hyperbolic groups; the coarse conjecture, not the group conjecture.
events.remains: The group conjecture.
events.direction: Coarse analogue; no direction on the group conjecture.

events.what_happened: Wang, Xie, Yu and Zhu, 'ℓ^p-coarse Baum-Connes conjecture for ℓ^q-coarse embeddable spaces', arXiv:2411.15070 (v1 22 Nov 2024; v2 26 May 2025, minor revision). Proves the ℓ^p version of the coarse Baum–Connes conjecture for spaces that coarsely embed into ℓ^q, for all p, q in [1, ∞).
events.delivers: A positive result for the coarse ℓ^p assembly map on spaces coarsely embeddable into ℓ^q; a coarse analogue, not the group conjecture.
events.remains: The group conjecture; coarse spaces outside the ℓ^q-coarse-embeddable class.
events.direction: Positive for the coarse analogue only.

events.what_happened: Cap, Harrach and Julg, 'Poisson transforms, the BGG complex, and discrete series representations of SU(n+1,1)', arXiv:2402.08262 (v1 13 Feb 2024; v2 8 Oct 2026, accepted for publication in J. Math. Inst. Jussieu per the v2 comment). Constructs Poisson transforms from differential forms on S^{2n+1} to complex hyperbolic space, realises discrete series of SU(n+1,1) on forms on the sphere, and states that the work is motivated by Julg's program. It claims no case of the Baum–Connes conjecture; the first part is said to apply in cases where the conjecture is open.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 13 Feb 2024; v2 8 Oct 2026 (small corrections; journal acceptance noted).
events.delivers: Analytic and representation-theoretic statements in Julg's program; no Baum–Connes case established.
events.remains: The conjecture in every case.

checked_by.who: Journal of Mathematical Institute of Jussieu (named on the arXiv v2 comment)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for publication (per the v2 comment; the journal page was not opened)

events.direction: No bearing on the conjecture's status.

events.what_happened: Jianguo Zhang, arXiv:2506.18446, first posted 23 June 2025 as 'The Baum-Connes conjecture for extensions revisited'. Version 1 claimed that for an extension 1→N→Γ→Γ/N→1 the conjecture with coefficients passes to Γ when it holds for N and Γ/N (its Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 3.13). Version 2 (23 August 2025, retitled 'A localization algebra approach to the Baum-Connes conjecture for extensions') instead assumes the conjecture with coefficients for the preimages q^-1(F) of finite subgroups F of Γ/N and for Γ/N, and presents the result as a known one (Oyono-Oyono's theorem) reproved by a localization-algebra method. The v2 acknowledgements thank Ralf Meyer and Shintaro Nishikawa for pointing out an essential mistake in Theorem 3.13 of v1; Remark 3.14 says the simpler condition is not true in general, citing Meyer's counterexample.
events.revisions: v1 23 Jun 2025 ('revisited'); v2 23 Aug 2025 (retitled; Theorem 3.13 hypotheses strengthened; Remark 3.14 concedes the N-only version).
events.delivers: Version 2: conditional permanence with coefficients: if Γ/N and each q^-1(F) satisfy the conjecture with coefficients in A, so does Γ. Restricted to that conditional form and presented as a known result, so no new group class. Version 1's N-only claim is not established (withdrawn in substance in v2).
events.remains: The conjecture for Γ whenever the hypotheses on Γ/N and on the preimages of finite subgroups are not verified; the coefficient-free statement for general extensions.

checked_by.qualification: Specialists in the Baum–Connes conjecture and K-theory of C*-algebras
checked_by.what_they_did: Identified an essential mistake in Theorem 3.13 of version 1, as acknowledged in version 2. This is an acknowledgement, not a published referee report

events.doubts: Version 1's N-only sufficiency claim was wrong, as the author concedes in version 2 Remark 3.14 and as Meyer's counterexample shows (arXiv:2508.05726). I did not read the proof of version 2's Theorem 4.5 or its localisation argument, so the correctness of version 2's statement rests on the author's revision and no independent check.

withdrawn.what: Version 1's claim that the conjecture with coefficients for Γ follows from N and Γ/N alone (Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 3.13 of v1); v2 replaces it with the finite-subgroup-preimage hypothesis and concedes the simpler condition is false in general.

events.direction: Positive, conditional permanence (version 2). Version 1's contrary claim is refuted.

events.what_happened: Ralf Meyer, 'The Baum-Connes conjecture for extensions', arXiv:2508.05726 (v1 7 August 2025; v2 29 August 2025), published Münster J. Math. 18 (2025) 245–247 (the journal's receipt and acceptance dates, 7 and 11 August 2025, come from a search summary of the journal PDF, which I did not open). The note shows that Chabert and Echterhoff's permanence hypotheses for extensions cannot be reduced to the N-only hypothesis Zhang claimed, and that an intermediate claim about direct products in Zhang's paper is false.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 7 Aug 2025; v2 29 Aug 2025; Münster J. Math. 18 (2025).
events.delivers: Refutes the claimed simplification (BC with coefficients for N alone suffices for an extension). The counterexample is with coefficients: a group G×Z/p (p prime), with coefficient algebra A⊗B, for which the assembly map with coefficients is not an isomorphism, though the maps for G (with A⊗B) and for Z/p are. It does not claim a counterexample to the conjecture itself, with or without coefficients, beyond the Higson–Lafforgue–Skandalis base.
events.remains: Everything about the conjecture for general groups; the refuted simplification is the only thing settled.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the note for publication (receipt and acceptance dates per search summary of the journal PDF; the PDF was not opened)

events.directly_checkable: The counterexample is a K-theory computation for an explicit group G×Z/p and coefficient algebra; the three steps (Lemma 1, the Künneth argument with Izumi's K-theory of B⋊Z/p, and the two isomorphisms) can be followed from the note's text. The base algebra A is inherited from the 2002 HLS construction and is not explicit in the part I read.
events.direction: Against a claimed simplification of an extension permanence hypothesis, in the coefficient setting. Not against the coefficient-free conjecture.
events.object: A countable discrete group G×Z/p with coefficient algebra A⊗B, where A is the separable G-C*-algebra from the Higson–Lafforgue–Skandalis counterexample and B = O_2⊗K(ℓ²N) carries a Z/p action. The assembly map with coefficients A⊗B for G×Z/p is shown not to be an isomorphism (the K-theory of the mapping cone is nonzero, via a Künneth argument and Izumi's computation K_0(B⋊Z/p) ≅ Z[1/p, ϑ], K_1 = 0), while the maps for G and for Z/p are isomorphisms. The existence of A is non-constructive in the HLS sense; the K-theory argument is explicit.

events.what_happened: Nishikawa and Petrosyan, 'Dehn fillings, equivariant homology, and the Baum–Connes conjecture', arXiv:2509.15070 (v1 18 September 2025; v2 8 October 2025, adding corollaries on Anderson-type Einstein manifolds and mapping class groups). Two results: (a) an excision sequence for classifying spaces for proper actions in equivariant homology, linking Cohen–Lyndon triples to the left-hand side of the conjecture; (b) the Baum–Connes conjecture with coefficients in the finite-wreath-product version holds for all discrete hyperbolic groups (building on Lafforgue), and with permanence and Dahmani–Guirardel–Osin's work, for a broad class including all real rank one lattices.
events.delivers: A variant: the finite-wreath-product form of the conjecture with coefficients, for hyperbolic groups and a class including real rank one lattices. The standard (non-wreath) statement is not claimed in the abstract. Per Lajoinie-Dodel's introduction, this is a stronger result for a larger class of relatively hyperbolic groups than that preprint's.
events.remains: The standard conjecture for groups outside these classes; the coefficient-free statement for groups beyond the hyperbolic and real rank one lattice cases.
events.direction: Positive for the wreath-product variant; no direction on the standard statement.

events.what_happened: Kitsios, Schick and Vigolo, 'Coarse Baum-Connes and warped cones: failure of surjectivity in odd degree', arXiv:2504.21811 (v1 30 April 2025; v2 22 May 2025, minor corrections and more detail). Abstract: 'We prove a conjecture of Roe by constructing unified warped cones that violate the coarse Baum-Connes conjecture', with the obstruction in odd rather than even degree. The result was presented in talks by Vigolo (Newton Institute, Cambridge, 9 October 2025) and Schick (Marseille, 9 October 2025; Bonn, 2 December 2025); those talks are listings, not reviews.
events.delivers: The coarse Baum–Connes conjecture fails for unified warped cones (non-compact metric spaces built from discrete group actions on compact manifolds), with the coarse assembly map not surjective in odd degree. It concerns the coarse assembly map on metric spaces, not the group assembly map; the abstract does not mention the group map.
events.remains: The group assembly map for every discrete group, which is the whole of the bullet.
events.direction: Against the coarse analogue only.
events.object: Unified warped cones: non-compact metric spaces built from a discrete group acting on a compact manifold, for which the coarse assembly map fails to be surjective in odd degree. Talk abstracts say the failure relies on spectral-gap-type properties of the metric spaces. The main theorems were not read; this comes from the arXiv abstract and talk listings.

events.what_happened: Gimperlein and Goffeng, 'Sharp mapping properties of Poisson transforms and the Baum-Connes conjecture', arXiv:2512.10018 (v1 10 December 2025; v2 7 April 2026, 'examples improved'). Proves a sharp quantitative analogue of Helgason's conjecture for the Knapp–Wallach Szegö map on semisimple Lie groups of real rank one (Sobolev spaces from van Erp–Yuncken's Heisenberg calculus), with commutators with C^∞ functions on the Furstenberg compactification compact. The abstract says this 'proves the remaining open conjecture in Julg's seminal program to establish the Baum-Connes conjecture for closed subgroups of semisimple Lie groups of real rank one'. The introduction states the program's aim as the conjecture with coefficients for all closed subgroups of real rank one groups, and attributes the representation-theoretic conjecture to Julg–Nishikawa.
events.delivers: Per the authors: completes the analytic step of Julg's reduction, so the conjecture (with coefficients, per the program's aim; hence also the coefficient-free case) for closed subgroups of real rank one groups. The introduction names earlier cases: Kasparov (SO(n,1)), Julg–Kasparov (SU(n,1)), Julg (Sp(n,1)). Which real rank one cases are new is not stated in the part of the text I read.
events.remains: The conjecture for all discrete groups outside the closed subgroups of real rank one groups, including higher-rank lattices such as SL(3,Z).
events.doubts: (1) The completion depends on Julg's reduction: the Fredholm-module step (Julg 2016) and the representation-theoretic step (Julg–Nishikawa 2021). I did not verify the published status of Julg's program. (2) I read about 100,000 of about 182,000 characters; the introduction's statement of which real rank one groups are new was not in that part. (3) Julg's January 2025 IHP talk abstract does not say whether the full proof is complete (search summary), and no source I found confirms the claim beyond the authors' own abstract.
events.direction: Positive, for a class of groups (closed subgroups of real rank one groups), with coefficients per the program's aim.

events.what_happened: Lajoinie-Dodel, 'Strong bolicity and the Baum-Connes conjecture for relatively hyperbolic groups', arXiv:2512.21169 (submitted 24 December 2025; v1 only). Constructs a strongly bolic metric for a class of relatively hyperbolic groups including those with CAT(0) or virtually abelian parabolics. If the parabolics also satisfy rapid decay (RD), Lafforgue's theorem gives the Baum–Connes conjecture for these groups. The introduction calls this 'a partial answer to this question in the case where the parabolic subgroups are CAT(0)'. Corollary 1.3 is stated without coefficients. The author gave talks (Paris-Saclay GT Groupes, 13 April 2026; an IMJ operator algebras seminar); those listings are not reviews.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 24 Dec 2025; no later version listed.
events.delivers: The conjecture without coefficients for relatively hyperbolic groups hyperbolic relative to CAT(0) parabolic subgroups that satisfy RD. Virtually abelian parabolics appear in the abstract's metric construction, but the conjecture is deduced only under RD on the parabolics.
events.remains: Relatively hyperbolic groups whose parabolics are not CAT(0), or do not satisfy RD; every other discrete group.
events.doubts: (1) Single-author preprint with no journal reference or public review found. (2) Whether this class was already covered is not established: the introduction calls the result partial, and my search for an earlier relatively hyperbolic Baum–Connes result (Mineyev–Yaman) returned nothing confirmed. The judging pass should check whether the Nishikawa–Petrosyan variant or earlier coarse-to-group arguments already cover this class. (3) Only about 100,000 of about 155,000 characters of the text were read; the section on the parabolic assumptions (Section 5.2) was cut off.
events.direction: Positive, for a class of relatively hyperbolic groups, in the coefficient-free form.

events.what_happened: Jianguo Zhang, 'The Baum-Connes and the Mishchenko-Kasparov assembly maps for group extensions', arXiv:2601.09615 (submitted 14 January 2026; v2 29 June 2026). Abstract: if the Baum–Connes assembly map is an isomorphism for the preimages of finite subgroups of Γ/N, then its injectivity, surjectivity and isomorphism pass from Γ/N to Γ; under a rational assumption on N, rational injectivity of the Mishchenko–Kasparov map passes; for isometric semidirect products N⋊G, results under three partial conjectures along N. Applications: closure of the strong Novikov, surjective assembly and Baum–Connes-with-coefficients properties under direct products, central extensions and finite extensions. Remark 4.12 notes that a hypothesis of Theorem 4.11 is strictly weaker than a condition of Theorem 3.15 for certain coefficients, citing Meyer's example.
events.revisions: v1 14 Jan 2026; v2 29 Jun 2026 (no changelog visible in the text I read).
events.delivers: Conditional permanence results: for extensions, with coefficients, under the finite-subgroup-preimage hypothesis (Theorem 1.2); rational Novikov under a rational hypothesis on N (Theorem 1.3); semidirect products under three partial conjectures (Theorem 1.5). No unconditional new group class in the text I read.
events.remains: The conjecture for Γ whenever these hypotheses fail to be verified; the coefficient-free conjecture for general groups.
events.doubts: The same author's earlier version of the extension permanence claim was wrong (arXiv:2506.18446, withdrawn in substance in v2). Remark 4.12 engages with Meyer's example, so the current version has been revised in response to it, but I did not confirm from the acknowledgements or the unread part of the text that no other change is needed.
events.direction: Positive, conditional permanence with coefficients; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Kai Mao, 'A going-down principle for étale groupoids and the Baum-Connes conjecture', arXiv:2602.19787 (v1 23 February 2026; v2 30 June 2026). A going-down principle for étale groupoids; it recovers Bönicke–Proietti's result on split injectivity of the Baum–Connes assembly map for groupoids strongly amenable at infinity, and gives applications to continuity of topological K-theory and to Künneth formulas. The paper states it does not prove the conjecture.
events.delivers: Groupoid-level: a going-down principle and split injectivity for groupoids strongly amenable at infinity, recovering a 2022/2024 result. Not a group result.
events.remains: Surjectivity and isomorphism for groupoids, and the group conjecture.
events.direction: Groupoid analogue; no direction on the group conjecture.

events.what_happened: Guo, Wang and Yao, 'The K-theory of maximal and reduced Roe algebras for Hecke pairs with equivariant coarse embeddings', arXiv:2601.14682 (v1 21 January 2026; v2 2 February 2026). Generalises the Dirac-dual-Dirac method to Hecke pairs with equivariant coarse embeddings, establishes K-theoretic isomorphisms between maximal and reduced equivariant Roe algebras, and extends these to prove the Baum–Connes conjecture in that setting.
events.revisions: v1 21 Jan 2026; v2 2 Feb 2026 (title changed between versions per the search summary).
events.delivers: A variant: the conjecture for Hecke pairs with equivariant coarse embeddings. The abstract does not say whether the group case is a special case, nor whether coefficients are included.
events.remains: The group conjecture as the bullet states it, unless the Hecke-pair setting contains it as a special case, which the abstract does not state.
events.direction: Variant (Hecke pairs); no direction on the group conjecture established.

events.what_happened: Shih-Yu Chang, 'The Unitary Conjugation Groupoid as a Universal Mediator of the Baum–Connes Assembly Map', arXiv:2603.22162 (v1 23 March 2026; one version; no journal reference). The abstract says the assembly map factors canonically through the unitary conjugation groupoid, which is a universal intermediary; for amenable crossed products the descent construction agrees with the analytic assembly map; and the K1 index framework extends to non-Type I examples such as the irrational rotation algebra.
events.delivers: A factorisation (framework) of the assembly map; the agreement with the analytic map for amenable crossed products, which is a known setting. Not a new case of the conjecture, per the abstract's framing.
events.remains: The conjecture for all discrete groups.
events.direction: Framework; no direction on the group conjecture.

events.what_happened: Three manuscripts in this family bear on the coefficient-free reduced assembly map (target C*_r(G), coefficient algebra C). (1) 'A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum-Connes injectivity' (dated 23 September 2026) constructs a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group Γ, an injective homomorphism i: Z^2 -> Γ, and a class c in H^2(BΓ; Z) with <(Bi)^*c, [T^2]> = 1, such that i_*(β) = 0 in K_0(C*_r Γ), where β is the rank-zero Bott generator of K_0(C*_r Z^2). Hence h = (Bi)_*[D_{T^2}] in K_0(BΓ) has infinite order, while its reduced assembly image is zero: a nonzero degree-zero kernel element of the reduced assembly map. (2) 'An irrational-trace counterexample to reduced Baum-Connes' (23 September 2026) constructs a finitely generated discrete group Γ_sur = V ⋊ Γ, with V a finite-field module, and a projection b_0 in C*_r(Γ_sur) whose canonical trace is the series sum over i of p^(-k_i), which the manuscript shows is irrational. Every class in the image of degree-zero assembly has rational trace (Lück's trace theorem, as recalled in the text), so [b_0] in K_0(C*_r Γ_sur) lies outside the image: a failure of surjectivity in degree zero. The manuscript states this refutes the coefficient-free reduced conjecture for countable discrete groups. (3) 'A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison-Kaplansky projection conjecture' (23 September 2026) is about projections, not assembly: it constructs a finitely generated torsion-free Γ_proj = Γ_base * F_N and a projection e in C*_r(Γ_proj) with 0 < τ(e) < 1/2. Its introduction and conclusion add a remark, not a numbered theorem, that the same small trace places [p_0] in K_0(C*_r Γ_base) outside the image of degree-zero coefficient-free reduced assembly for the finitely generated torsion-free Γ_base, citing Baum-Guentner-Willett Prop. 10.3. That is a second, remark-level surjectivity failure in degree zero. (The same manuscript also disproves the Kadison-Kaplansky projection conjecture, which is not a matched problem here.)
events.delivers: Injectivity fails in degree zero for the coefficient-free reduced assembly map, witnessed by one finitely generated torsion-free group (manuscript 1). Surjectivity fails in degree zero, witnessed by one finitely generated discrete group (manuscript 3, stated as a theorem); manuscript 2 gives the same kind of failure for Γ_base as a remark. Because the bullet asks that the assembly map be an isomorphism in every degree, a failure in degree zero alone refutes it as stated, under the bullet's reading (every discrete group, coefficient C, both injectivity and surjectivity). The manuscripts say so: manuscript 1 says it disproves rational injectivity of the coefficient-free reduced assembly map for torsion-free groups; manuscript 3 says the coefficient-free reduced Baum-Connes conjecture for countable discrete groups is false. Their statement of the conjecture matches the bullet's coefficient-free reading: assembly from equivariant K-homology of the proper classifying space to K_j(C*_r G), for j = 0, 1, with trivial coefficient C. Restrictions: manuscript 1's counterexample is torsion-free and fails only injectivity, in K_0. Manuscript 3's group is not claimed torsion-free; V is an F_p-vector space, so Γ_sur has elements of finite order. The bullet does not require torsion-freeness, so this does not weaken the refutation of the bullet as stated. Manuscript 3's failure is shown in K_0 only.
events.remains: Nothing is left to refute in the bullet's stated reading: degree zero already refutes it. Not addressed by any of the three manuscripts: (i) degree one, K_1, of the coefficient-free reduced map; (ii) the version with coefficients in a separable G-C*-algebra, which the bullet does not name and which these manuscripts do not treat; (iii) the maximal assembly map, which manuscript 1 says still detects its class (mu^max(h) tensor 1 is nonzero), so it does not refute the maximal version; (iv) the status of the surjectivity failure for Γ_base in manuscript 2, which is a remark-level claim and not a numbered theorem.
events.doubts: (1) Manuscript 1's group is a finitely generated subgroup obtained from an infinite construction by a finite-witness lemma, so the text establishes existence of the group rather than exhibiting it. (2) Manuscript 1's abstract says rational injectivity is disproved for torsion-free groups; its theorem gives one group, which is enough for the universal statement, and the kernel element has infinite order, so the abstract and theorem agree. (3) Manuscript 1's maximal-side discussion records a gap in the all-groups version of the cited Antonini-Buss-Engel-Siebenand result and says it uses the corrected, finitely presented version; the authors say the reduced claim does not depend on it. (4) Manuscript 3's group is not claimed torsion-free, although the abstract's phrase 'for countable discrete groups' suggests a general scope; the theorem gives one group. (5) Manuscript 3's surjectivity conclusion depends on Lück's trace theorem, which is cited, and not on the paper's own analysis. (6) Manuscript 2's surjectivity claim for Γ_base is a remark with a citation, not a proved theorem in its own right. A search of the section files for hedges (sketch, conjecture, assume, erratum, and similar) found no step flagged as sketched in the BC-relevant claims, beyond the items listed here.; conditional on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed in manuscript 1's reduced theorem or manuscript 3's surjectivity theorem, beyond their own constructions and cited published results. Cited results used but not reproved: manuscript 1 uses the twisted spin Dirac index theorem [AS63], in the dimension-two form of [BvE16, Thm. 1], the Emerson-Hudson assembly formula for the torus [EH20, Thm. 1.3], which identifies the assembly image of the torus Dirac class with the rank-zero Bott generator, and the geometric-to-analytic K-homology comparison [BHS07, Thms. 6.1-6.2]. Its maximal-side remark (μ^max(h) tensor 1 nonzero) rests on Hanke-Schick and on a corrected statement of Antonini-Buss-Engel-Siebenand; the reduced claim does not use these. Manuscript 3 uses Lück's trace theorem (Theorem 0.3 of Lück 2002) as a black box for rationality of traces on the assembly image, with the direct-limit domain convention stated in the text; it also uses Osajda's labelling theorem (Theorems 2.7 and 3.2) and Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak expanders. Manuscript 2's surjectivity remark depends on Baum-Guentner-Willett Prop. 10.3 and on Lück's integrality result; its projection theorem does not depend on them.
events.direction: disproves the conjecture: injectivity fails in degree zero (manuscript 1); surjectivity fails in degree zero (manuscript 3; remark-level in manuscript 2)
events.object: No explicit group is written down. In each case the group comes from an existence argument: expanders with large girth, codes over F_p or sampled voltages, Osajda-type labellings, and, in manuscript 1, a finite-witness lemma that extracts a finitely generated subgroup of an infinite construction. The manuscripts say finite presentation is not part of the conclusion. The explicit objects are: in manuscript 1, the degree-zero class h = (Bi)_*[D_{T^2}] in K_0(BΓ), of infinite order and in the kernel of reduced assembly; its vanishing is shown by proof, not by formula. In manuscript 3, the projection b_0 = 1_{0}(T), the spectral projection at zero of an explicit finite-field-module operator T in C*_r(Γ_sur), with trace sum over i of p^(-k_i), where the k_i are chosen with increasing gaps. In manuscript 2, the projection e is given by an explicit compression formula from p_0, but its base group Γ_base is existence-selected.

disputes.summary: Zhang's version 1 (arXiv:2506.18446) claimed the conjecture with coefficients passes to an extension from N and Γ/N alone. Meyer's counterexample (arXiv:2508.05726) refutes this, and version 2 concedes it (Remark 3.14) and replaces the hypothesis with a condition on preimages of finite subgroups. Zhang's 2026 paper (arXiv:2601.09615) continues the line and cites Meyer's example in Remark 4.12.

Lajoinie-Dodel (arXiv:2512.21169) and Nishikawa–Petrosyan (arXiv:2509.15070) treat overlapping classes of relatively hyperbolic groups, in different versions of the conjecture (coefficient-free in the first, finite-wreath-product with coefficients in the second). Lajoinie-Dodel's introduction describes the Nishikawa–Petrosyan preprint as independent and simultaneous. This is an overlap, not a dispute; no claim of priority is made in either source that I read.

summary: Across about 58 searches and about 25 opened sources, I found no resolution, no counterexample and no AI-generated result for the coefficient-free Baum–Connes conjecture for all discrete groups since 26 January 2024. The Wikipedia article (last edited 10 January 2026) says 'The conjecture without coefficients is still open' and names SL(3,Z) as the simplest open case. What did move in the window is class-level. Lajoinie-Dodel (arXiv:2512.21169, December 2025) deduces the coefficient-free conjecture for relatively hyperbolic groups whose parabolics are CAT(0) and satisfy rapid decay, which the author calls a partial answer. Gimperlein and Goffeng (arXiv:2512.10018, December 2025) say they complete the analytic step of Julg's program, which by the program's stated aim gives the conjecture with coefficients for closed subgroups of real rank one groups; their introduction names earlier cases for SO(n,1), SU(n,1) and Sp(n,1). The extension-permanence line (Zhang, June 2025 and January 2026) is with coefficients and is conditional. Its version 1 was wrong, as Meyer's counterexample (August 2025, published in Münster J. Math.) shows and the author concedes in version 2. Nishikawa and Petrosyan (September 2025) prove a finite-wreath-product variant for hyperbolic groups and a class including real rank one lattices. The analogues are the coarse counterexample for warped cones (Kitsios–Schick–Vigolo, April 2025), the positive ℓ^p coarse result (Wang–Xie–Yu–Zhu, November 2024), the groupoid going-down principle (Mao, February 2026), the Hecke-pair result (Guo–Wang–Yao, January 2026), and a framework paper (Chang, March 2026). Pre-window events are recorded as well, including the 2002 Higson–Lafforgue–Skandalis counterexample, which is to the version with coefficients. Close calls: (a) Gimperlein–Goffeng. Read as settling a class, it changes the picture for real rank one closed subgroups; but it depends on Julg's program, whose published status I could not verify, and the introduction's list of new cases was not in the part of the text I read. (b) Lajoinie-Dodel. Read as a new class, it moves the coefficient-free question; but I could not confirm an earlier result covering the same class, and the Section 5.2 assumptions were cut off in the part I read. Read as a partial answer it does not move the statement for general groups. (c) Nishikawa–Petrosyan and Zhang's extension results are with coefficients or in a variant form, so a reader who takes the bullet as the coefficient-free statement should not count them as moving it. (d) The 2002 counterexamples are to the version with coefficients, so they do not bear on the coefficient-free bullet unless one reads the bullet with coefficients. AI: no source credits an AI system with any Baum–Connes result. I searched the AI angle directly (OpenAI's Astra 'Ten advances' list of 1 August 2026, GPT-5 Pro and Gemini Deep Think claims, Erdős and open-problem trackers, Lean formalisation and arXiv AI-disclosure questions). The Astra list, as reported by secondary sources, includes a disproof of Connes's rigidity conjecture in operator algebras but no item on K-theory or assembly maps; the primary OpenAI page returned HTTP 403, so that list rests on secondary reports. One aggregator reports an Anthropic statement that a public Claude model reproduced about half of the Astra results. That is unverified and concerns the Astra list, not this problem. 'none_found' is recorded as true on each event because no system is named in any Baum–Connes source I read. For the long papers (Gimperlein–Goffeng, Zhang 2026, Lajoinie-Dodel) I read most of the text but not the final acknowledgements, so that is a limit on the 'none found' claim.
competing_reading: The problem moved in a restricted way within the window. Lajoinie-Dodel's theorem and the Gimperlein–Goffeng claim each settle the coefficient-free conjecture for a class of groups (relatively hyperbolic groups with CAT(0) RD parabolics; closed subgroups of real rank one groups), and a reader who counts class-level settlements would record a moved problem with no AI involvement. The opposing reading is that the bullet asks for every discrete group, and no source claims more than a class, so the problem is unchanged: the Wikipedia article's January 2026 revision still calls it open, and the 2002 counterexamples and the 2025 Zhang–Meyer work concern the version with coefficients, not this one.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full texts of Gimperlein–Goffeng and Lajoinie-Dodel, to read the introduction's statement of which groups are new, whether the real rank one result is with coefficients, and the Section 5.2 parabolic assumptions. (2) Confirmation of the published status of Julg's program (Julg 2016 Fredholm module; Julg–Nishikawa 2021; the 2025 analytic step) from the journals. (3) An expert survey or a later paper stating which classes the coefficient-free conjecture covers in 2026, in particular whether Lajoinie-Dodel's class was already covered by earlier results. (4) The OpenAI primary 'Ten advances' page, to confirm that none of its ten items concerns K-theory or assembly maps.

Deng–Toyota and other coarse-geometry papers in the window beyond those recorded.

Not addressed by any of the three manuscripts: (i) degree one, K_1, of the coefficient-free reduced map; (ii) the version with coefficients in a separable G-C*-algebra, which the bullet does not name and which these manuscripts do not treat; (iii) the maximal assembly map, which manuscript 1 says still detects its class (mu^max(h) tensor 1 is nonzero), so it does not refute the maximal version; (iv) the status of the surjectivity failure for Γ_base in manuscript 2, which is a remark-level claim and not a numbered theorem.
event.doubts: (1) Manuscript 1's group is a finitely generated subgroup obtained from an infinite construction by a finite-witness lemma, so the text establishes existence of the group rather than exhibiting it. (2) Manuscript 1's abstract says rational injectivity is disproved for torsion-free groups; its theorem gives one group, which is enough for the universal statement, and the kernel element has infinite order, so the abstract and theorem agree. (3) Manuscript 1's maximal-side discussion records a gap in the all-groups version of the cited Antonini-Buss-Engel-Siebenand result and says it uses the corrected, finitely presented version; the authors say the reduced claim does not depend on it. (4) Manuscript 3's group is not claimed torsion-free, although the abstract's phrase 'for countable discrete groups' suggests a general scope; the theorem gives one group. (5) Manuscript 3's surjectivity conclusion depends on Lück's trace theorem, which is cited, and not on the paper's own analysis. (6) Manuscript 2's surjectivity claim for Γ_base is a remark with a citation, not a proved theorem in its own right. A search of the section files for hedges (sketch, conjecture, assume, erratum, and similar) found no step flagged as sketched in the BC-relevant claims, beyond the items listed here.; conditional on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed in manuscript 1's reduced theorem or manuscript 3's surjectivity theorem, beyond their own constructions and cited published results. Cited results used but not reproved: manuscript 1 uses the twisted spin Dirac index theorem [AS63], in the dimension-two form of [BvE16, Thm. 1], the Emerson-Hudson assembly formula for the torus [EH20, Thm. 1.3], which identifies the assembly image of the torus Dirac class with the rank-zero Bott generator, and the geometric-to-analytic K-homology comparison [BHS07, Thms. 6.1-6.2]. Its maximal-side remark (μ^max(h) tensor 1 nonzero) rests on Hanke-Schick and on a corrected statement of Antonini-Buss-Engel-Siebenand; the reduced claim does not use these. Manuscript 3 uses Lück's trace theorem (Theorem 0.3 of Lück 2002) as a black box for rationality of traces on the assembly image, with the direct-limit domain convention stated in the text; it also uses Osajda's labelling theorem (Theorems 2.7 and 3.2) and Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak expanders. Manuscript 2's surjectivity remark depends on Baum-Guentner-Willett Prop. 10.3 and on Lück's integrality result; its projection theorem does not depend on them.
event.direction: disproves the conjecture: injectivity fails in degree zero (manuscript 1); surjectivity fails in degree zero (manuscript 3; remark-level in manuscript 2)
event.object: No explicit group is written down. In each case the group comes from an existence argument: expanders with large girth, codes over F_p or sampled voltages, Osajda-type labellings, and, in manuscript 1, a finite-witness lemma that extracts a finitely generated subgroup of an infinite construction. The manuscripts say finite presentation is not part of the conclusion. The explicit objects are: in manuscript 1, the degree-zero class h = (Bi)_*[D_{T^2}] in K_0(BΓ), of infinite order and in the kernel of reduced assembly; its vanishing is shown by proof, not by formula. In manuscript 3, the projection b_0 = 1_{0}(T), the spectral projection at zero of an explicit finite-field-module operator T in C*_r(Γ_sur), with trace sum over i of p^(-k_i), where the k_i are chosen with increasing gaps. In manuscript 2, the projection e is given by an explicit compression formula from p_0, but its base group Γ_base is existence-selected.

judgement.why: The statement is the coefficient-free assembly map being an isomorphism for every group, so with-coefficients, coarse, groupoid, Hecke-pair and wreath-product results are variants, and permanence/programme papers (Oyono-Oyono, Zhang, Meyer, Julg steps, Čap–Harrach–Julg, Chang) settle nothing about the statement itself. Class-level proofs (Haagerup, hyperbolic, Lie-group classes, and in-window Gimperlein–Goffeng and Lajoinie-Dodel) are cases. The OpenAI family claims an explicit failure of injectivity and of surjectivity of the coefficient-free reduced map in degree zero for specific groups; one such group refutes a universal isomorphism claim, so it is scored whole/refuted/counterexample, unreviewed, and doubtful rather than not_credible because 8 days is too short to expect uptake and no error is identified. The README quote says the model obtained the results, so generated.
judgement.doubts: The record's 'delivers' for openai-math-285 swaps manuscript numbers 2 and 3 relative to 'what_happened' (which manuscript states surjectivity as a theorem); the injectivity failure in manuscript 1 stands either way. The README quote is repository-wide ('vast majority of results'), not specific to this family. Gimperlein–Goffeng and Lajoinie-Dodel may partly overlap earlier-known classes; scored case regardless. Wassermann and Chabert–Echterhoff–Nest concern Lie groups, scored case since the statement names no group class.
